thread:
simon: Heads-up: saw a p99 spike on canary this morning after the kernel swap and microbatching tweak. Profiling attached (summary below). Anyone seen KV-warmup interactions like this before?

emma: ugh. can you paste the profile snip? is this 1) new kernel change, 2) different microbatch sizing, or 3) traffic shift?

simon: short version: we moved from kernel-A to kernel-A-opt (better matmul path for long sequences) + reduced microbatch target from 8->4 to reduce queue latency. Overall throughput looked fine, but tail jumped for a subset of requests. paste: 
```
perf summary: p50 42ms, p95 110ms, p99 420ms (baseline p99 ~180ms)
flame: KV lookup hot on first call, stall ~120ms waiting on microbatch fill for small seqs
kernel: optimized matmul path shows faster token emit for long seqs
```

jia: That smell like KV cache warmup + microbatch convoying. If smaller microbatches -> less KV amortization. Some requests hit cold KV and wait for batch to fill.

rohan: Also check the kernel's cold path: kernel-A-opt may have a heavier init/dispatch for short seqs. Optimizations often trade steady-state perf for higher fixed overhead.

perf-ci: automated test: replayed live traffic from last week vs synthetic poisson. Replay reproduced the p99 regression reliably; synthetic loads (uniform/concurrent clients) did not.

emma: that's key. replay captures the inter-request spacing and seq-length distribution. Synthetic often hides convoying. We need a hybrid: replay + targeted synthetic microbursts.

simon: Agreed. Two debate points: 1) Measurement target — do we report p95 or p99 for SLOs here? customers care about p99 for interactive app. 2) Benchmark methodology — can we trust replay results if the replay infra doesn't simulate client-side backoff and real multiplexing?

jia: For SLOs: p95 is useful for capacity planning, but p99 is the real user-visible tail. I'd keep p99 for alerts and p95 for daily dashboards.

rohan: On replay fidelity: replay must preserve arrival times, connection multiplexing, and KV warmup state. We should snapshot KV state beforehand (or explicitly test cold vs warm scenarios). Otherwise replay underestimates tails.

ops-bot: FYI: opened issue #1423 to add KV snapshot support to replay harness and an opt-in cold-start test matrix.

perf-ci: proposal: three-pronged bench run per kernel change: (A) steady-state synthetic for throughput, (B) replay of prod traces for tail, (C) synthetic microburst + cold-KV to exercise worst-case tail. Automate gating: if p99 increases >2x or delta >100ms block rollout.

emma: +1. Also add microbatch histograms (batch sizes over time) and per-request KV-hit flag so we can correlate tail samples to cold hits.

jia: quick workaround: increase microbatch target to 6 for the canary pool to see if tails vanish. If they do, we know it's amortization. but that's a knob, not a fix.

simon: I'll roll the microbatch knob on canary and re-run replay. If stable, revert kernel swap and run debug build with extra tracing to isolate kernel init overhead.

rohan: one more: check our kernel selection heuristics — we currently pick kernel-A-opt for avg seq > 256. Maybe the selector is mis-classifying some short-heavy routes. Add per-route telemetry.

emma: action items: simon toggle microbatch (canary), perf-ci run replay+microburst with KV snapshot, rohan add per-route kernel telemetry, ops-bot link issue. We'll reconvene after results. :thumbsup:

simon: thanks — will post quick results in this thread.
